blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Per-head-SHA group (dmtools-agents#682, live fa#1202/#1203 on
  # 2026-10-03 23:05–23:57; still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22 —
  # eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave,
  # fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010). The fa #911 fix below stopped
  # the IN-FLIGHT kills, but the global group kept killing the PENDING
  # ones: a queued run in a shared concurrency group ALWAYS supersedes
  # the pending one ("Any existing pending job or workflow in the same
  # concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued
  # job or workflow will take its place" — GitHub docs);
  # cancel-in-progress: false only shields the RUNNING run. So every
  # silent-refresh push / factory-data snapshot / dev-wave push cancelled
  # every other branch's pending kicker, the required contexts
  # (sm-liveness/head-completeness where a repo requires them) ended
  # CANCELLED on fresh PR heads, and the PRs sat BLOCKED until manual
  # reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone).
  # Scoping the group to the pushed head SHA means no push can displace
  # another push's kicker: a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a
  # tick ALWAYS gets to run. The kicker jobs stay seconds-cheap and
  # idempotent (liveness re-probes before dispatching, head-completeness
  # re-checks with a 45s grace), so wave-time parallel kickers are
  # harmless — same cost posture as the fa #911 "let them queue" call.
  # cancel-in-progress stays false: even a same-SHA collision (schedule
  # + manual dispatch on one commit) must never kill an in-flight kicker.
  # CONSUMERS: re-pin your stub to this commit. If your stub defines its
  # OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too (or drop
  # it — this group now carries the scoping): a caller-level global
  # group re-introduces the pending-run supersession on its own.
  group: factory-sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # Real tick, always: the workflow_dispatch default is dryRun=true
            # (a safety default for HUMAN dispatches). A bare dispatch from the
            # kicker lands dry and cannot merge anything — live evidence
            # 2026-10-03: dart kicker fired within 7s of #340's checks but the
            # SM ran "(dry)" (runs 37152253853, 37157212391); every merge that
            # night rode manual -F dryRun=false ticks instead.
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -F dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.guestReworkMaxAttempts — cap on guest validation-red rework arms per
 *   PR (review #701; default 2). Counted via the 'guest rework arm N/MAX' marker
 *   lines appended to the guest fail reports; at N >= MAX the arm is withheld and
 *   the coordinator owns the PR.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering
 *   workflowFile   (optional) — GitHub Actions workflow file  (default: ai-teammate.yml)
 *   workflowRef    (optional) — git ref for dispatch           (default: main)
 *   concurrencyKey (optional) — workflow concurrency key override (default: ticket key)
 *   projectKey     (optional) — value passed as the `project_key` workflow input so the runner
 *                               activates the correct project-specific dependency setup (e.g. "myproject",
 *                               "bice"). Auto-derived from configPath basename when not set
 *                               (e.g. ".dmtools/configs/myproject.js" → "myproject").
 *   skipIfLabel    (optional) — skip ticket if it already has this label (idempotency)
 *   skipIfLabels   (optional) — skip ticket if it already has any of these labels
 *   addLabel       (optional) — add this label after triggering (idempotency marker)
 *   addLabels      (optional) — add these labels after triggering
 *   recoverStaleTriggerLabel (optional) — if true, remove skip labels when no matching
 *                               active workflow exists and continue processing. Trigger
 *                               labels that are also added by the same rule recover by
 *                               default; set false to opt out.
 *   enabled        (optional) — set to false to disable the rule entirely (default: true)
 *   limit          (optional) — max number of tickets to process per run (default: 50)
 *   localExecution (optional) — if true, run postJSAction directly (no runner, no AI/CLI)
 *   localTeammate  (optional) — if true, run the full teammate pipeline (checkout, AI CLI,
 *                               PR/Jira actions) synchronously in-process via
 *                               scripts/run-teammate-local.sh instead of dispatching a
 *                               GitHub Actions workflow_dispatch. Tickets are processed
 *                               strictly one at a time (the local checkout is reused across
 *                               tickets, so no concurrency/workflowBudget accounting applies).
 *                               Secrets are read from the calling shell's environment or from

**gh-748 fix — SM side (this repo):**

At the `validate_pr` dispatch decision point, after the existing duplicate-dispatch guard finds no active dispatched run:
1. **Registration-lag grace**: wait briefly and re-probe with a WIDENED query before committing to the dispatch. The widened query: ANY run on the head_sha (any workflow, any event, any triggering actor), counting pending/queued/in_progress/waiting as active — completed runs within a short grace also count (a just-concluded kicker may have ordered CI that hasn't registered yet... hmm, actually a completed run doesn't order CI *after* completing; the CI dispatch happens during the run. If CI was dispatched during the kicker run, the CI run registers within seconds — covered by the wait. So completed runs of OTHER workflows shouldn't count — only active ones matter for the widened probe. Wait — but what about a completed CI run within the last seconds? `hasActiveDispatchedRun`'s 15-min completed grace already covers completed CI runs. For the widened probe (registration lag re-probe), active-only is the right semantics: the lag affects runs dispatched seconds ago, which would show as queued/pending once registered — active.)

Hmm wait, actually there's one more subtle case for the widened probe: the kicker run COMPLETED 5 seconds ago having dispatched CI at its very end; the CI run hasn't registered yet (lag). The widened ACTIVE-only probe sees nothing (kicker is completed, CI not registered) → SM dispatches → duplicate! To close THAT, the widened probe would also need to count recently-COMPLETED runs of the kicker... but the kicker run completed having NOT dispatched (code-bearing head) → SM would wrongly skip → +1 tick latency for fresh code-bearing heads... 

Ugh. Trade-off again. Let me quantify the race direction though: in the live incident, the kicker dispatched at 17:45:51 and the SM probed at ~17:45:53 with the run NOT visible. The kicker itself was STILL IN FLIGHT at that point (started 17:45:28, sleep 45 means it dispatched at ~17:46:13... hmm, that doesn't add up with the ticket's timeline — the ticket says the kicker's grace re-check ran at 17:45:32, 4s after start. So at incident time the kicker had a ~4s grace, not 45s; the 45s sleep was likely added later (the current external code says "45s grace" — and the current code re-checks ALL CI runs, no status filter, post-grace). Anyway: at probe time, the kicker was IN FLIGHT.)

So the live race shape: **kicker in-flight → kicker's CI dispatch fired → not yet registered → SM probed → miss → duplicate.** The widened ACTIVE probe catches this: the in-flight kicker run is visible on the head → skip. And the "completed kicker that just ordered CI" sub-case: the CI run it ordered registers within seconds of the kicker's completion; if the SM probes in that sub-second window... the widened probe misses. But that window is tiny (registration happens server-side within ~1-2s), and the PRIMARY observed lag was 2-4s on a just-fired dispatch — hmm, wait, that contradicts: if registration takes only 1-2s, why was the run invisible 2-4s after dispatch?

Actually the registration lag for `gh workflow run` is known to be up to ~10-20s sometimes (the run needs to be created in the Actions backend; the API list endpoint lags). The observed gap: dispatch 17:45:51, SM's probe maybe at 17:45:53-54, SM's own dispatch at 17:45:55. So the run was invisible ≥3s after dispatch. 

For the "completed kicker" sub-case, the same lag applies to the CI run it ordered: kicker completes at T, CI dispatched at ~T-2s (before its final step completes? Actually `gh workflow run` is the last command of the kicker's last step — the run completes ~1s after dispatch). So CI dispatch at ~T-1s, invisible until T-1+lag. SM probes at T+1s: widened ACTIVE probe → kicker completed (not active), CI not registered → MISS → duplicate. Hmm! So counting ONLY active runs in the widened probe still leaves the just-completed-kicker window open, roughly equal to the registration lag.

To close it fully: count runs of ANY workflow that are active OR completed within a SHORT grace (60s per the ticket) — the just-completed kicker counts → skip. Cost: code-bearing head whose kicker completed <60s ago → SM skips → next tick (≤10 min later) dispatches. How often does a tick land within 60s after a push? Pushes happen at some rate; SM ticks every 10 min. P(a given fresh head's tick lands within 60s of its push) is low-ish, but across a busy train... Each such head gets +≤10 min validation latency. vs. the duplicate cost: 2x CI per raced push on a single-runner setup = potentially HOURS of queue latency. The ticket explicitly directs: "count ANY run on the head_sha (pending/queued included, any triggering actor) as 'already dispatched', with a short grace (60s) for API visibility lag." So the ticket wants ANY run (any status within the grace window, pending/queued included, any actor) → already-dispatched.

OK so I'll follow the ticket direction literally:

**New probe: `hasAnyRecentHeadRun(repoInfo, headSha, graceMs)`** (name TBD) — ANY run on the head (any workflow, any event, any actor):
- active (queued/in_progress/waiting/pending) → true
- completed within graceMs (default 60_000) of updated_at → true
- else false; fail OPEN (false) on probe error (consistent with the other guards — worst case the duplicate we're preventing, never a wedge).

```

```
Hmm wait — but should this widened check run on EVERY validate_pr dispatch (every fresh code-bearing push)? Then every push whose kicker completed <60s before the tick defers a tick. As computed, that's the ticket's accepted cost. Hmm, hmm. Let me reconsider ONE more time whether to count completed runs...

Actually wait — re-read the ticket's wording ONE more time: "count ANY run on the head_sha (pending/queued included, any triggering actor) as 'already dispatched', with a short grace (60s) for API visibility lag."

"pending/queued included" — this phrase suggests the baseline is "runs" in some status set and the ticket clarifies pending/queued count too. "with a short grace (60s) for API visibility lag" — the grace covers visibility lag. I now think the intended composite semantics is exactly: any run on the head, in ANY status, counts as already-dispatched when it is either (a) still active, or (b) completed within the last 60s (the visibility-lag grace: a run that completed seconds ago may have ordered CI that isn't registered yet — and for the kicker specifically, its CI child registers seconds after the kicker's own completion). Also (c) — a run with created_at within the last 60s?? Hmm no.

Hmm — one more consideration: why 60s for completed runs and 15 min for the CI workflow's own completed runs? Because a COMPLETED CI run within 15 min already counts via hasActiveDispatchedRun (the existing probe — vProbe.active covers it). The widened probe only needs to cover NON-CI runs (the kicker) + lag. For non-CI runs, 60s of post-completion relevance is right: after that, if the kicker had ordered CI, the CI run is long registered and vProbe.active/15-min grace owns it.

But hold on — active runs of the CI workflow: already covered by vProbe.active. Active runs of OTHER workflows (kicker in flight): widened probe catches → skip. Should an in-flight kicker really block? YES …

Live: fa ai/gh-1292 (PR #1295), 2026-10-05 17:45 — TWO CI workflow_dispatch runs 4s apart (#37350859642 queued 17:45:51, #37350866965 pending 17:45:55).

Root cause — two dispatchers cover the same head state with no shared 'already ordered' marker:
1. Kicker push-handler (run 37350806830, 17:45:28): saw codeless head with zero required contexts; its grace re-check for in-flight CI ran at 17:45:32 — SM had not dispatched yet → kicker dispatched CI.
2. SM tick (run 37350542834, started 17:43:24): validate-fresh matched the same PR (checks none/pending); validate_pr's hasActiveDispatchedRun duplicate guard probed before the kicker's workflow_dispatch run was visible via the API (registration lag) → fail-open → second dispatch at 17:45:55.

Cost: 2x CI per raced push — with a single live runner this directly doubles queue latency for the whole train.

Fix directions (pick one or both):
- SM validate_pr: count ANY run on the head_sha (pending/queued included, any triggering actor) as 'already dispatched', with a short grace (60s) for API visibility lag.
- Kicker: skip the codeless-head CI dispatch when the head belongs to a PR carrying ai_validating (the SM owns validation of armed heads).

Regression test: simulated push + concurrent tick → exactly one CI run on the head.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:

  # eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave,
  # fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010). The fa #911 fix below stopped
  # the IN-FLIGHT kills, but the global group kept killing the PENDING
  # ones: a queued run in a shared concurrency group ALWAYS supersedes
  # the pending one ("Any existing pending job or workflow in the same
  # concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued
  # job or workflow will take its place" — GitHub docs);
  # cancel-in-progress: false only shields the RUNNING run. So every
  # silent-refresh push / factory-data snapshot / dev-wave push cancelled
  # every other branch's pending kicker, the required contexts
  # (sm-liveness/head-completeness where a repo requires them) ended
  # CANCELLED on fresh PR heads, and the PRs sat BLOCKED until manual
  # reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone).
  # Scoping the group to the pushed head SHA means no push can displace
  # another push's kicker: a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a
  # tick ALWAYS gets to run. The kicker jobs stay seconds-cheap and
  # idempotent (liveness re-probes before dispatching, head-completeness
  # re-checks with a 45s grace), so wave-time parallel kickers are
  # harmless — same cost posture as the fa #911 "let them queue" call.
  # cancel-in-progress stays false: even a same-SHA collision (schedule
  # + manual dispatch on one commit) must never kill an in-flight kicker.
  # CONSUMERS: re-pin your stub to this commit. If your stub defines its
  # OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too (or drop
  # it — this group now carries the scoping): a caller-level global
  # group re-introduces the pending-run supersession on its own.
  group: factory-sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

/**

 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.guestReworkMaxAttempts — cap on guest validation-red rework arms per
 *   PR (review #701; default 2). Counted via the 'guest rework arm N/MAX' marker
 *   lines appended to the guest fail reports; at N >= MAX the arm is withheld and
 *   the coordinator owns the PR.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the

# gh-748: Double CI dispatch: kicker push-handler races SM validate-fresh (~20s window, fa ai/gh-1292)

## Description

Live: fa ai/gh-1292 (PR #1295), 2026-10-05 17:45 — TWO CI workflow_dispatch runs 4s apart (#37350859642 queued 17:45:51, #37350866965 pending 17:45:55).

Root cause — two dispatchers cover the same head state with no shared 'already ordered' marker:
1. Kicker push-handler (run 37350806830, 17:45:28): saw codeless head with zero required contexts; its grace re-check for in-flight CI ran at 17:45:32 — SM had not dispatched yet → kicker dispatched CI.
2. SM tick (run 37350542834, started 17:43:24): validate-fresh matched the same PR (checks none/pending); validate_pr's hasActiveDispatchedRun duplicate guard probed before the kicker's workflow_dispatch run was visible via the API (registration lag) → fail-open → second dispatch at 17:45:55.

Cost: 2x CI per raced push — with a single live runner this directly doubles queue latency for the whole train.

Fix directions (pick one or both):
- SM validate_pr: count ANY run on the head_sha (pending/queued included, any triggering actor) as 'already dispatched', with a short grace (60s) for API visibility lag.
- Kicker: skip the codeless-head CI dispatch when the head belongs to a PR carrying ai_validating (the SM owns validation of armed heads).

Regression test: simulated push + concurrent tick → exactly one CI run on the head.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

  # eight branches' kicker runs cancelled inside one 36-second dev-wave,
  # fa run ids 37182568709…37182598010). The fa #911 fix below stopped
  # the IN-FLIGHT kills, but the global group kept killing the PENDING
  # ones: a queued run in a shared concurrency group ALWAYS supersedes
  # the pending one ("Any existing pending job or workflow in the same
  # concurrency group, if it exists, will be canceled and the new queued
  # job or workflow will take its place" — GitHub docs);
  # cancel-in-progress: false only shields the RUNNING run. So every
  # silent-refresh push / factory-data snapshot / dev-wave push cancelled
  # every other branch's pending kicker, the required contexts
  # (sm-liveness/head-completeness where a repo requires them) ended
  # CANCELLED on fresh PR heads, and the PRs sat BLOCKED until manual
  # reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone).
  # Scoping the group to the pushed head SHA means no push can displace
  # another push's kicker: a queued kicker that is about to dispatch a
  # tick ALWAYS gets to run. The kicker jobs stay seconds-cheap and
  # idempotent (liveness re-probes before dispatching, head-completeness
  # re-checks with a 45s grace), so wave-time parallel kickers are
  # harmless — same cost posture as the fa #911 "let them queue" call.
  # cancel-in-progress stays false: even a same-SHA collision (schedule
  # + manual dispatch on one commit) must never kill an in-flight kicker.
  # CONSUMERS: re-pin your stub to this commit. If your stub defines its
  # OWN caller-level concurrency group, scope it per-head too (or drop
  # it — this group now carries the scoping): a caller-level global
  # group re-introduces the pending-run supersession on its own.
  group: factory-sm-kicker-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \

          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine logins ride the
      # deployment-level input (#687, gh-728), exactly like the factory's
      # contract. Comma-separated LIST: the agent harness bot AND the CI
      # bot — github-actions[bot] authors its own PRs (live fa PR #1249)
      # and must ride the machine path (owner directive 2026-10-05).
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot]'
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

/**
 * SM Agent — Scrum Master automation (JSRunner)
 *
 * Reads an array of rules from params.rules (defined in agents/sm.json)
 * and for each rule:
 *   1. Queries Jira by rule.jql (with {jiraProject}/{parentTicket} interpolation)
 *   2. Optionally transitions each ticket to rule.targetStatus
 *   3. Runs the agent for each matching ticket, via one of three modes:
 *      - dispatch (default) — triggers an ai-teammate GitHub Actions workflow (async)
 *      - localExecution: true — runs the agent config's postJSAction directly in the
 *        SM process (pure JS, no AI CLI, no checkout — for fast/safe operations)
 *      - localTeammate: true — runs the FULL teammate pipeline (checkout/branch switch,
 *        AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) synchronously on the local machine via
 *        scripts/run-teammate-local.sh, one ticket at a time (no GitHub Actions runner)
 *
 * Configuration:
 *   Loads project config from .dmtools/config.js (via configLoader).
 *   If config.smRules is provided, uses those instead of params.rules (full override).
 *   Repository owner/repo from config override params when present.
 *   JQL placeholders {jiraProject} and {parentTicket} are resolved from config.
 *   jobParams.maxTriggeredWorkflows (or maxWorkflowsPerRun) limits total active plus newly
 *   dispatched workflows across all non-local rules.
 *   Override priority: config.smMaxWorkflows (from .dmtools/config.js) > sm.json value.
 *   jobParams.forceLocalTeammate — set via a CLI JSON override (note the outer `params`
 *   wrapper — `dmtools run <file> <override>` deep-merges into the whole {name, params}
 *   job config, not directly into params.jobParams; a bare {"jobParams":{...}} override
 *   is silently ignored):
 *   `dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'`
 *   to switch EVERY default-dispatch rule to the local teammate pipeline for that run,
 *   without editing sm.json/.dmtools/config.js. Rules with localExecution:true are
 *   unaffected; a rule can still opt out with an explicit `localTeammate: false`.
 *   jobParams.guestReworkMaxAttempts — cap on guest validation-red rework arms per
 *   PR (review #701; default 2). Counted via the 'guest rework arm N/MAX' marker
 *   lines appended to the guest fail reports; at N >= MAX the arm is withheld and
 *   the coordinator owns the PR.
 *   jobParams.redHeadSkip = false — OWNER ESCAPE HATCH (directive 2026-10-04 "red yields
 *   the slot"): disables the validate-arm red-head skip. Recording of red heads on the
 *   fail reports continues (audit trail); only the arm-side skip goes dark. A rule can
 *   also opt out alone with rule.redHeadSkip = false. jobParams.redHeadCap (default 3)
 *   tunes how many reds on the SAME head SHA block the re-arm.
 *   jobParams.emptyLapMax (default 1, review #703 retune — was 2) — after this many
 *   consecutive EMPTY rework laps on the same head (a lap that closes itself successful
 *   without moving the head — live fa#1211 run 37196297279), fail_validation withholds
 *   the agent:rework arm, posts an owner escalation, and the report says a human owns
 *   the PR. Reachability: withholding fires on the (emptyLapMax + 2)-th red on the
 *   head, so it is only live while redHeadCap >= emptyLapMax + 2 (3 >= 1 + 2 at the
 *   defaults — with the old emptyLapMax=2 the arm-side red-head skip killed the 4th
 *   same-head validation first and the cap was dead code).
 *
 * Rule fields:
 *   jql            (required) — JQL to find tickets (supports {jiraProject}, {parentTicket})
 *   configFile     (required) — agents/*.json to pass as config_file workflow input
 *   configPath     (optional) — path to a project config (.dmtools/config.js) for this rule
 *                               overrides the global config; enables multi-project orchestration
 *   description    (optional) — human-readable label shown in logs
 *   targetStatus   (optional) — Jira status to transition tickets to before triggering
 *   workflowFile   (optional) — GitHub Actions workflow file  (default: ai-teammate.yml)
 *   workflowRef    (optional) — git ref for dispatch           (default: main)
 *   concurrencyKey (optional) — workflow concurrency key override (default: ticket key)
 *   projectKey     (optional) — value passed as the `project_key` workflow input so the runner
 *                               activates the correct project-specific dependency setup (e.g. "myproject",
 *                               "bice"). Auto-derived from configPath basename when not set
 *                               (e.g. ".dmtools/configs/myproject.js" → "myproject").
 *   skipIfLabel    (optional) — skip ticket if it already has this label (idempotency)
 *   skipIfLabels   (optional) — skip ticket if it already has any of these labels
 *   addLabel       (optional) — add this label after triggering (idempotency marker)
 *   addLabels      (optional) — add these labels after triggering

 *                               labels that are also added by the same rule recover by

# gh-748: Double CI dispatch: kicker push-handler races SM validate-fresh (~20s window, fa ai/gh-1292)

## Description

Live: fa ai/gh-1292 (PR #1295), 2026-10-05 17:45 — TWO CI workflow_dispatch runs 4s apart (#37350859642 queued 17:45:51, #37350866965 pending 17:45:55).

Root cause — two dispatchers cover the same head state with no shared 'already ordered' marker:
1. Kicker push-handler (run 37350806830, 17:45:28): saw codeless head with zero required contexts; its grace re-check for in-flight CI ran at 17:45:32 — SM had not dispatched yet → kicker dispatched CI.
2. SM tick (run 37350542834, started 17:43:24): validate-fresh matched the same PR (checks none/pending); validate_pr's hasActiveDispatchedRun duplicate guard probed before the kicker's workflow_dispatch run was visible via the API (registration lag) → fail-open → second dispatch at 17:45:55.

Cost: 2x CI per raced push — with a single live runner this directly doubles queue latency for the whole train.

Fix directions (pick one or both):
- SM validate_pr: count ANY run on the head_sha (pending/queued included, any triggering actor) as 'already dispatched', with a short grace (60s) for API visibility lag.
- Kicker: skip the codeless-head CI dispatch when the head belongs to a PR carrying ai_validating (the SM owns validation of armed heads).

Regression test: simulated push + concurrent tick → exactly one CI run on the head.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
